messages:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing p99 east-west interconnect latency spikes in the us-west GPU pool during the 09:00-09:15 batching window. Tail jumps to ~30-60ms, occasional drops.

sasha: saw the same on cluster-3. A few model-serving pods queue up and backpressure that makes burst latency worse.

kevin: any recent config changes? MTU, RDMA driver, firmware?

alex: not that I know of. No deploys flagged for the plane. Monitoring shows NIC tx drops and RX errors increasing in the same window.

monitoring-bot: alert: netlatency-high - notify: #eng-infra - metric: east_west_p99 > 25ms for 3m (clusters: cluster-2, cluster-3).

jamie: can someone grab ethtool -S + ifconfig/mtu on the affected nodes and an ibstat for RDMA? Also tcpdump on the NIC for a sample peak.

alex: quick grab from one node (shortened):
```
$ ifconfig eth0 | grep mtu
eth0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>  mtu 9000
$ ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_over_errors|tx_aborted"
rx_errors: 0
rx_over_errors: 112
tx_errors: 0
tx_aborted_errors: 18
$ ibstat
CA 'mlx5_0'
  CA type: MT4115
  Port 1: State: Active
  Link layer: InfiniBand
```

kevin: rx_over_errors count during the window is suspicious. Could be buffer bloat at ToR or a NIC offload interaction (GRO/GSO) with RDMA path.

niraj: did we have jumbo frame changes? MTU shows 9000 which is expected. But we've seen intermittent fragmentation when a mix of VMs had older drivers.

alex: ran a quick experiment: disabled GRO/GSO on one victim node during the next window — p99 dropped to ~12-18ms but CPU on host rose ~6%.

jamie: that suggests offload splitting packets late in the stack causing retransmits or reassembly pauses. Could also be NIC firmware RX ring pressure. Any queue length deltas?

alex: qdisc shows occasional tcp_tx_timeout and tx_queue_len spikes around the same timestamps.

kevin: ok. Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) pin high-batching inference traffic to same rack (avoid east-west hops) 2) disable GRO/GSO on hosts handling the worst batches 3) patch ToR NIC firmware + check buffer sizing.

niraj: agree. I'll schedule a controlled experiment: disable GRO/GSO on two nodes in cluster-3 during next peak, leave others as baseline. Also collect pcap and ethtool -S trending.

monitoring-bot: note: created incident trace id=inc-2026-418 for correlation.

alex: FYI we also saw an RDMA retransmit counter tick on mlx5, but not full failure. Could be a transient congestion window collapse when batching bursts align.

jamie: can we rate-limit or smooth batch dispatch in the serving runtime as a temporary software control? That reduces throughput but might avoid synchronized bursts.

alex: I enabled a 5ms jitter on a canary deployment (small fleet) at 09:30. Result: p99 reduced ~40% on the canary routes, overall throughput unchanged for the fleet test.

kevin: nice. Opened INFRA-2345 for firmware + ToR buffer review, and INFRA-2346 for host driver inventory + recommended offload settings.

niraj: I'll attach tcpdumps and ethtool snapshots to INFRA-2346. Planning a maintenance window next Tue to roll driver updates across the pool.

alex: follow-up: we should add an autoscaling policy tweak so Dedicated pools avoid cross-rack packing during high batch windows until we have a permanent fix. That reduces tail latency hit for customers.

jamie: noted. I'll add a proposal to the ops-runbook and tag product for SLA messaging.

deploy-bot: rollout: canary batch-jitter applied to svc/model-serve-canary at 2026-06-12T09:30:22Z :white_check_mark:

kevin: thanks. Action items: niraj collects artifacts, jamie updates docs/runbook, kevin tracks firmware ticket, alex monitors next two peak windows and reports.

sasha: thanks team. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
